correctness.rationale: The displayed rational predator–prey reaction with diffusion diag(1,100) and Neumann length π√10 has homogeneous positive equilibrium u=v=h, with κ=(2−h)/(h(2+h)). Direct differentiation gives J(h)=[[1/2−h,−3/2+h²/4],[1/2,−1/2]], tr J=−h<0 and det J=(4+4h−h²)/8>0. At h_c=42−sqrt(43410)/5, D1(h_c)=0 (5h²−420h+138=0); n=0 and every n≥2 remain strictly stable. The critical right vector is (1,1/21), and reflection flips the first Neumann cosine. Hessian, third derivative tensor, and constant/second-harmonic inverses yield exact normal form dot t=S(κ−κ_c)t+Ct³+remainder with independently recomputed S≈0.113222629765>0, C≈−0.603782237456<0. Algebraic rational root isolation certifies signs, not mere floating-point signs. Standard analytic parabolic center manifold/implicit function theorem with spectral gap gives exactly two nearby positive, reflection-related, locally exponentially stable nonconstant equilibria for small κ>κ_c; no global result or all-parameter theorem is claimed.
residual_risks: Local small-κ−κ_c analytical theorem; no global attractor or other parameter ranges.
